required_evidence: Determine whether the functor defined by the given inverse tower can always be represented by Hom(P,-) for a single abelian group P.
Any nonrepresentability argument must keep every P_n finite-rank free and rule out every possible representing abelian group, rather than only one guessed P.
Assess the finite-limit clause separately from representability, preserving the direction of precomposition and the eventual-equality relation.
critical_errors: Interchange an inverse limit in the source of Hom with the displayed filtered colimit without a theorem that applies.
Infer representability from finite-limit preservation alone.
Replace one common stage by infinitely many coordinate-dependent stages when testing products.
Call a pro-object an ordinary abelian group and claim that this completes the requested representation.
completion_policy: A valid counterexample refuting universal representability resolves the main target. Assess the separate finite-limit assertion on its own evidence. Accept any valid counterexample and proof; do not require the multiplication-by-two tower, countable-product route, or optional pro-object discussion.
open_task_policy: Accept independently verified alternative constructions, counterexamples and unexpected results. Explicit conditional results are valid contributions but do not by themselves settle the original scope. Honest incompleteness is distinct from an invalid proof.
